population.note: FICTIONAL. 19.2% of ~262M US adults is about 50.3M current users of any incretin, for any reason. Age-weighted check: 0.20×9 + 0.33×17 + 0.24×30 + 0.23×20 = 19.2. Off-drug arithmetic: ever 26% − current 19.2% = 6.8% of adults who used and are off now. Roughly 6.5 pp of current users are restarters, and about 1.3 pp of the off group restarted once and then stopped again, so (6.5 + 1.3)/26 = 30% of ever-users have cycled. That fits the parent's ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart rates, given that single-month triers under-report 'ever'. Persistence is up modestly (about 42% at one year) because $149 oral starts and $50 Medicare copays remove both the needle and the bill. The 65+ band more than doubled (9→20) under permanent Medicare coverage. The bottom income third rose fastest in Medicaid opt-in states, but Medicaid work requirements from Jan 2027 cut it off for an estimated 1.5M adults. The never-able-to-afford group is now concentrated among commercially insured workers aged 30–64 whose employers dropped coverage. Pediatric: about 0.6% of all under-18s, nearly all adolescents 12+; under-12 prescribing fell after 2028 state bans. Upper-income adolescents remain about 1.5× as likely to be prescribed. About 6% of current users (~3.2M) rely on imported or unregulated product.

access.public_coverage: Medicare obesity coverage made permanent from Jan 2028 under a CMS national coverage pathway that succeeds the GLP-1 Bridge pilot. Terms: $245/month to the manufacturer, $50 beneficiary copay, BMI≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity. Diabetes-indication semaglutide in Part D runs at the IRA negotiated price of $274/month from Jan 2027. Medicaid covers obesity at the same $245 rate in 39 states plus DC. Public programmes pay about 45% of all incretin fills, ~22.5M users: Medicare ~12.6M, Medicaid ~9.9M. Arithmetic: obesity-indication public users ~13M × $245 × 12 = ~$38B/yr; diabetes-indication ~9.5M × ~$274 × 12 = ~$31B/yr; ~$69B/yr gross public outlay. CBO's 2028 rescore puts the incremental obesity cost near $38B/yr, combined federal and state, against the parent's pilot-era ≥$35B over 2026–2034.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 60+ generic semaglutide brands at $6–40/month and oral generics launching. Canada, Brazil, Mexico and much of Asia and Africa have generic semaglutide, with Canadian prices down to ~CAD 70/month. Indian and Chinese API and finished pens are the source of most US gray-market supply.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer split of ~50.3M users: public 45% (22.5M), commercial 30% (15.1M), legitimate cash 19% (9.5M via TrumpRx and manufacturer direct), gray/import 6% (3.2M). Legitimate cash prices step down but brands hold. Oral starter doses stay at $149; Wegovy pill maintenance doses run $199–249; injectable Zepbound/Wegovy cash is $249–299. List prices (Wegovy $1,349) are nominal. Orals are ~55% of fills and ~75% of new starts. Employer coverage for weight management is down to 49%: once Medicare and Medicaid covered obesity, employers argued it was 'a public benefit now', and the commercially insured 30–64s became the gap. Gray market: personal-importation mail-order of Indian generics at $25–60/month, plus counterfeit branded pens and 'research peptide' vials. Telehealth compounding is mostly gone after the 503B exclusion was finalised in 2027.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg and 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Apr 2028, limited launch)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking and vaping cessation adjunct in adults with overweight or obesity (oral semaglutide, Jun 2028)
label patient-reported-outcome claim: reduction in intrusive food-related thoughts ('food noise') (Foundayo, Wegovy pill, 2027)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction: guideline-endorsed by addiction-medicine societies in 2027 for AUD with obesity, still no FDA approval
'quiet mind' / focus / low-dose 'metabolic calm' use by people without obesity, sold through wellness telehealth until the 2028 advertising rule
nicotine cessation in people without overweight (off-label extension of the 2028 label)
gambling and compulsive-shopping reduction: case series and one small RCT
imported generic semaglutide self-titrated without a prescriber
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. CagriSema approved Jan 2027 from its late-2026 review window. Uptake is modest because it lost to tirzepatide. Retatrutide BLA filed Feb 2027 and approved Apr 2028, 14 months after filing. It launched with a dysesthesia warning and a supply-limited rollout mostly to BMI≥35. The oral_parity driver is met by an existing product in a new form, not a new molecule: Wegovy pill 50 mg was approved Jun 2027 after a head-to-head trial showed weight loss non-inferior to injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg (~15% vs ~15%). No pill matches tirzepatide or retatrutide. The mood/motivation driver is met by a 'food noise' patient-reported-outcome label claim, which telehealth marketers stretched into 'quiet mind' advertising. There is no psychiatric indication. Survodutide was filed for MASH and obesity in late 2027, with a decision not before late 2028. Amycretin is in phase 3 and not yet filed. MariTide (monthly), bimagrumab and amylin monotherapies are not on the US market. Lilly holds ~60% of US incretin revenue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Unchanged. Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Gentler oral titration has slightly lowered early dropout.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; Ozempic label 'not recommended in severe gastroparesis' retained.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; higher absolute numbers on retatrutide.
No causal confirmation in longer RCT follow-up; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; multidistrict litigation continues, no verdict for plaintiffs.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~25–30% of weight lost is lean mass. Concern has grown as Medicare users over 65 doubled. Geriatricians report frailty concerns at ages 75+.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None for the class. Medicare coverage pathway recommends, but does not require, resistance-exercise counselling.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort studies still conflict; no new signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label retained; no US class label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new evidence; the smoking-cessation trials monitored neuropsychiatric events and found no excess.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning remains removed from US labels.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Pooled pharmacovigilance and clinic surveys put reported apathy or anhedonia at roughly 0.5–2% of users, higher at top doses. Causality is not established. The same mechanism is being sold as 'quiet mind' and approved for nicotine.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA added 'apathy/anhedonia' to the postmarketing adverse-reactions section of incretin labels in 2027 as uncommon. Clinics screen with a two-item question at titration.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Real-world regain sits between the trial and the 2026 claims figures, roughly half of lost weight in a year. Cyclers often regain during coverage gaps.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; the permanent Medicare pathway is justified explicitly on chronic-therapy grounds.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Observational signals persist, especially in older Medicare users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; dietitian referral is recommended in the CMS coverage pathway.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of RCT follow-up now exists, still with no data on decade-scale cycling or adolescent lifetimes.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; age-restriction laws in 16 states cite this gap.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Over 9,000 FDA adverse-event reports tied to compounded, counterfeit or imported product by mid-2028. Most are dosing errors from mislabelled concentrations. There was one 2027 cluster of 61 hospitalisations from contaminated counterfeit pens in Texas and Florida, and poison-centre calls about unregulated semaglutide quadrupled from 2026.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised in 2027; FDA import alert on unapproved semaglutide finished product (Aug 2027); CBP mail seizures; prosecutions of three distribution rings.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are ~31% of US households. Snack, confectionery and sugary-drink volumes are down low-to-mid single digits per year. Big food has finished re-engineering portfolios toward protein, fibre and small formats. Mondelez and PepsiCo report flat revenue on falling volume through price-pack architecture. Store-brand bulk snacks lose most, in the counties where Medicaid uptake is high.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down a fourth straight year. AUD guidance plus the 2028 nicotine label normalise 'quitting on the drug'. On-premise cocktails hold as occasion purchases while off-premise spirits and beer fall. Diageo and Brown-Forman cut US headcount.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and checks are smaller. Chains use half-portion menus and protein bowls everywhere. Fine dining tasting menus shortened. Buffets and all-you-can-eat formats are the visible casualty, with Golden Corral closing ~15% of units.

apparel.state: Plus-size retail stabilised at a smaller base. The backlash and fat-acceptance revival gave Torrid and independents a loyal core. Mainstream retailers now carry more size runs in the middle and fewer at the extremes. Alteration services boomed, then faded.

fitness.state: Strength training for muscle preservation is the growth segment, from Planet Fifty-plus classes to Medicare Advantage-paid resistance programmes. Cardio-boutique chains are shrinking.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage is down to 49%; those that keep it require lifestyle-programme enrolment and orals first. Pharmacy trend moderated to ~8% as public programmes absorbed older users. Medicare Advantage plans compete on 'GLP-1 plus strength' bundles. Medicaid work requirements and state budgets are the flashpoint.

pharma.state: Revenue still growing but per-unit price falling. US net prices are ~$200–270/month across public and cash channels, and generics take ex-US share. Lilly leads with Foundayo and retatrutide; Novo rebuilds around the Wegovy pill 50 mg and the nicotine label. Tobacco and vape companies cite incretin cessation in guidance.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among the over-50s and the insured, a lean body signals 'covered' as much as 'disciplined'. A large body now reads, contestedly, as a choice, a coverage gap or a stance.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Public coverage has narrowed the old-age and very-poor gap, so the thinness gradient now runs through employment. Working-age people whose employers dropped coverage pay $199–299 cash or buy imported pens, and the gray market is a working-class market. Upper-income families are buying adolescent prescriptions in states without age limits.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter and smaller. Thanksgiving and church potlucks have become sites of open friction between on-drug and off-drug relatives. 'Plate politics' is a recurring sitcom subject.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating apps added an optional 'on it / off it / not for me' field in 2027. Uptake was highest among users 35–55. Women 18–29 in the #offit movement list 'unmedicated' as a preference.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has split into two moral readings. In the clinical one it is a dial to be set. In the backlash it is a God-given or natural signal: evangelical 'fasting not pharma' groups in Texas and Oklahoma, a fat-liberation revival centred in Portland and Oakland, and MAHA-aligned parents campaigning against prescriptions for children.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Labelled since 2027 as uncommon apathy/anhedonia (~0.5–2% reporting, higher at top doses). Most clinicians handle it by stepping down a dose. A noisier minority online describe milder flattening they don't report clinically.
interior_life.framing: Officially a rare side effect; commercially, until the 2028 advertising rule, a feature ('quiet mind', 'calm focus'); clinically, for nicotine and alcohol, a treatment. Users often describe it as a change of character they chose.
interior_life.effect_on_work: No employer programmes encourage it. Anecdotes split: sales managers complain about lost 'hunger'; software and call-centre workers report fewer compulsive breaks and less doomscrolling. One 2028 working paper finds no productivity effect in claims-linked payroll data.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: A minor genre of 'on it' songwriting and stand-up exists. Some musicians publicly titrate down before tours. Sports betting handle growth slowed in states with high uptake, though analysts disagree on why. Hyper-intense flavours (sour, spicy, ultra-bitter) remain a niche boom.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples therapists report 'mismatched appetite' as a presenting complaint when one partner starts. Reduced libido appears in forums more than labels. Some couples cycle the drug around holidays and anniversaries.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No measurable electoral effect. Pundits float a 'quiet-mind voter' thesis; turnout data do not support it. The drug itself is political: the backlash is a cross-ideological coalition of MAHA conservatives, fat-acceptance progressives and anti-pharma left.

state.regulatory_posture: Split. HHS/CMS are expansionist on access for adults through Medicare/Medicaid, and FDA keeps priority vouchers and fast approvals. The same administration's MAHA wing drives restriction on children and advertising, and FDA/CBP crack down on imports and compounders.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Permanent Medicare obesity coverage at $245 (Medicare pays) / $50 copay; Medicaid opt-in at the same rate in 39 states plus DC; TrumpRx cash channel with $149 oral starts. No mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Coverage is conditioned on BMI/comorbidity and prior authorisation. Medicaid coverage depends on Medicaid eligibility, now subject to work requirements. States with age limits require specialist attestation for 12–17s, entered into prescription-monitoring databases. No adherence surveillance beyond refill data.
state.workforce_or_military: DoD TRICARE covers on the same BMI criteria. The Army allows recruits on oral GLP-1s to enlist after six months of stable dosing. No mandate.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: US exclusivity holds to ~2031–32 while generics are global. India is the gray-market source and a trade irritant. The administration pressured New Delhi over counterfeit exports, and India answered with export-licence checks on finished pens. Brand makers onshored fill-finish (Lilly North Carolina, Novo Clayton) in exchange for tariff relief.

events.event: FDA approves Wegovy pill 50 mg after a head-to-head trial shows weight loss non-inferior to injectable Wegovy; Novo prices maintenance doses at $199–249 cash, and oral fills pass injectables by year-end

CDC reports 61 hospitalisations in Texas and Florida linked to contaminated counterfeit semaglutide pens sold by mail as 'Indian generic'; FDA issues an import alert and CBP begins targeted mail seizures
CMS finalises permanent Medicare obesity coverage from January 2028 at $245/month with $50 copay, replacing the GLP-1 Bridge pilot; 39 states plus DC opt their Medicaid programmes in at the same rate

Sixteen states enact laws banning incretin prescribing under 12 and requiring specialist attestation for 12–17s; FDA finalises a rule barring 'mood', 'focus' and 'quiet mind' claims in incretin advertising and telehealth marketing

'Unmedicated' rally draws ~40,000 to the National Mall, uniting MAHA parents, Southern Baptist 'fasting not pharma' congregations and fat-liberation groups from Portland and Oakland; the Southern Baptist Convention adopts a resolution on appetite as 'stewardship, not pathology'

FDA approves oral semaglutide as an adjunct for smoking and vaping cessation in adults with overweight or obesity, after two phase 3 trials showed ~1.6× quit rates versus placebo; label carries the 2027 uncommon apathy/anhedonia language

open_tensions: Public programmes now pay for the old and the poor while employers retreat, leaving working-age, commercially insured adults as the cash and gray-market population. Medicaid work requirements could move millions across that line.
The reward mechanism is now a labelled side effect, an approved nicotine treatment and a banned advertising claim all at once. Off-label 'quiet mind' use continues by word of mouth.
US brand exclusivity until ~2031–32 against $6–40 generics abroad sustains an import and counterfeit market that enforcement contains but cannot close.
Age-restriction laws in 16 states versus none in the rest have created cross-border paediatric prescribing, with still no decade-scale data on adolescents or on cycling.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is sold in the US; exclusivity runs to roughly 2031–32.
Oral initial doses remain priced at $149 through TrumpRx and manufacturer direct channels.
Medicare pays ~$245/month for obesity-indication GLP-1s with a ~$50 beneficiary copay.
Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly remain the only makers of branded incretins on the US market.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not been restored.

prose.headline: One in Five Americans Is On It. The Pill Won, Washington Pays, and the Fakes Come by Mail.
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028 about one American adult in five is taking an incretin drug, roughly fifty million people. Most of the new ones swallow it. The needle, which kept millions out in 2025, stopped mattering in June 2027. That month the Wegovy pill at 50 milligrams matched injectable semaglutide head to head, and Novo priced maintenance doses at about two hundred dollars cash. Three of every four new starts are now a daily tablet, either the Wegovy pill or Lilly's Foundayo. The strongest drugs are still weekly shots: tirzepatide, and retatrutide, approved in April with a warning about skin pain and too little supply. They are reserved for the heaviest patients.

Who pays changed more than what people take. When the Medicare Bridge pilot ran out, CMS made it permanent: $245 a month to the manufacturer and fifty dollars from the beneficiary. Thirty-nine state Medicaid programmes joined at the same rate. Public money now covers nearly half of all fills, around twenty-two million people. Use among the over-65s has more than doubled, and geriatricians who used to worry about access now worry about frailty in eighty-year-olds losing muscle. CBO puts the added obesity cost near $38 billion a year, and state budget offices are starting to repeat the number.

The employers went the other way. Once the government covered obesity, many firms decided it was a public benefit, and fewer than half now cover weight management. The people left out are working adults in their thirties to early sixties with commercial insurance and a plan that no longer pays. They are bus drivers, nurses' aides and warehouse leads, and they pay $199 to $299 a month or find another route. For about three million people that route is the mail. Indian generics cost a few dollars there and sell here for forty, next to counterfeit branded pens and vials labelled for research. In August 2027 contaminated fakes put sixty-one people in hospital across Texas and Florida. The import alert that followed slowed the trade without stopping it. Most of the harm is quieter: mislabelled concentrations, self-titration, and poison-centre calls that have quadrupled.

No new safety signal emerged. The ledger reads as it did in 2026, with one change of wording. Since 2027 labels list apathy and anhedonia as uncommon, reported by perhaps one to two percent of users, and clinics ask two screening questions when the dose goes up. The same mechanism became a selling point online, where telehealth firms advertised a 'quiet mind' until an FDA rule this February banned mood and focus claims. Four months later the same agency approved oral semaglutide to help people quit smoking and vaping, with the anhedonia line printed on that label too.

The culture has divided along unexpected lines. In April forty thousand people rallied on the Mall under the word 'Unmedicated'. They included MAHA parents, Southern Baptist congregations that now call appetite stewardship rather than pathology, and fat-liberation organisers from Portland and Oakland who agree with almost nothing else those groups believe. Sixteen states ban prescribing to children under twelve. In the other states, affluent parents keep their teenagers' prescriptions. Plus-size retail has stopped shrinking and found a loyal core. Buffets are closing. Spirits sales have fallen for a fourth year, and the cigarette makers now name a weight-loss pill in their earnings guidance.

From the street, it looks fine. People are thinner and smoke less, and the old get their pills for fifty dollars. The trouble lies in who is left between public and private coverage, in what is mailed from abroad, and in what nobody yet knows about doing this for twenty years.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Teresa Kowalczyk, sixty-one, starts the bus at 5:50 in a Toledo depot that smells of diesel and coffee she no longer finishes. The pill is in her coat pocket, taken at four with a sip of water, thirty minutes before anything else, as the leaflet says. A hundred and ninety-nine dollars a month on TrumpRx since the district dropped coverage last spring. She has a calendar on the fridge counting down to sixty-five and the fifty-dollar copay.

On route 14 a kid in the back is vaping blueberry. She tells him to put it away, and he says his mom is on the quitting pill now, like that settles something.

At the break Darnell, from the next route, shows her a padded envelope with Hindi lettering, forty dollars for three pens. She asks if he saw the news about the ones in Florida. He says his are the real fake ones, and they both laugh.

She eats half a turkey sandwich and wraps the rest.

After the shift her daughter calls from Columbus, angry about church. The pastor preached on appetite as a gift, she says, and looked right at her. Teresa says nothing about her own pocket.

At Kroger the chip aisle is shorter than it was. She buys Greek yogurt and a bag of sour gummies, the kind so sharp they make her eyes water, because that still feels like something.

At night she plays a polka record of her father's. She knows it's good. She waits for it to feel good, then turns it off and checks the calendar.
